rows.title: bad output: empty-findings chunks, agy Markdown shapes and the read-coverage floor (R1, R3, R4)
rows.note: R1 a chunk answering {"findings":[]} recorded as bad output; R3 agy Markdown shapes rejected (bare file lists, clean phrasing); R4 the read-coverage floor discarded answers that had findings. Narrowed on 2026-09-29 from the whole word to the three texts those mechanisms printed: any other bad output is its own problem. 2026-10-01 regression (2 opus-high legs, rounds 20260930T002018Z-a9fe8ce and 20260930T115302Z-c1f76ba): the floor priced text with nothing left to read, clean verdicts only, never a finding. The a9fe8ce chunk was a 192 KB menu dump (llm-legs docs/handoffs/menu-consistency/menu-before.txt), already unpriced by the base's pending `data_bytes` (scope.py DATA_DUMP_SUFFIXES). The c1f76ba chunks were whole files of a `--files` hunt pasted into the prompt, refused after one grep: a scope whose every file the commit adds outright (or is a dump) and whose diff the prompt carries now prices nothing (scope.py whole_text, launch.py _record_prompt). An edited file's chunk and a prompt without the diff keep the floor. Shared cause of both fixes: the floor's base is the diff's bytes, which overprices text the cell holds whole or that is no code.

rows.title: a cross-repository brief named its second repository only in prose, so worker-run granted it nothing and every write there read as escaped
rows.note: x8 claudeb legs 2026-09-29/30 (hammerspoon, claude-setup, logo-vectorizer-bench): every brief listed its second repository in prose (Working directories / Repos / Workdirs) and no relay or flag carried it, so add_dirs stayed empty; worker-run now grants a header ADD-DIR: line as --add-dir. The detail names the files-note outside-write class, the narrowest the leg carries: a write to a repository no brief names still lands here and reads as a regression. 2026-10-01: six packet regressions inspected: five omit grants for prose-authorized claude-setup/review-bench writes; one grants the review-bench sibling but explicitly pours into ungranted llm-legs main. Fresh doctor additionally counts a grantless review-bench resume. Fixture header parsing passes for fresh/resume, prose grants nothing. Current doctor/vendor brief emitters and night-sweep resume guidance already carry ADD-DIR; do not duplicate them. Scratch filtering does not explain the reported repository paths. Historical launcher revision remains unconfirmed (B3). Relay/scope owner handoff required; no authorized claude-setup worktree.

rows.title: a codex family the catalog resolved to no slug crashed its cells instead of ending pool empty
rows.note: x2 sol-high cells of round 20260930T021101Z-8810740 (borodatch, burkhartor): `codexb models --family sol` printed nothing, most likely because the refusal store skipped gpt-6.1-sol pool-wide after its 01:36 UTC refusal (rollout lag); codex_account_serves swallowed the resolver's ValueError and run_codex raised it again. The family word is now recorded unlisted for every account, so the cell ends `pool empty` with `codex model sol is not served by any account`, as shared-invariants row cv says. The trigger, the refusal store itself, is proposed for removal in docs/handoffs/2026-09-30-codex-refusal-store-removal.md (llm-legs and review-bench together).

rows.title: Claude JSON error result omitted from worker failure diagnostics
rows.note: claudeb-1790757454-79915-4251 on com: exit 1, empty err, nonempty JSON/result says Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed; is_error true despite subtype success. Fixture reproduces no output; feeding the error to current vocabulary yields unclassified, ruling out an evidence-source-only fix. No recorded watchdog/memory kill or missing vendor answer. OAuth refresh cause unconfirmed in retained out/result/err; no credentials opened or refresh attempted. Shared auth vocabulary correction needs review-bench, outside authorized worktrees. Matcher is the narrowest available emitted model/detail, not proof every matching future run has this cause.
